title.en: State the classical, statistical and axiomatic definitions
Use combinations to count favourable cases

say.en: We say a die shows six with probability one-sixth. We can reason it out from equally likely faces, or roll the die thousands of times and count. Both roads lead to the same number. In this lesson: State the classical, statistical and axiomatic definitions.
Use combinations to count favourable cases.

body.en: *Classical* (Laplace): if an experiment has n exhaustive, mutually exclusive and equally likely outcomes, m of which favour A, then $P(A) = m/n$. Statistical (von Mises): $P(A) = \lim_{n\to\infty} m/n$, the limit of the relative frequency in n repeated trials. Axiomatic (Kolmogorov): $P(A) \ge 0$, $P(S) = 1$, and $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)$ for mutually exclusive A, B.
body.kn: ಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯ: n ಸಮಸಂಭವ, ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ, ಸಮಗ್ರ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ m ಅನುಕೂಲವಾದರೆ P(A) = m/n. ಸಾಂಖ್ಯಿಕ: ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಅನಂತದತ್ತ ಸಾಗಿದಾಗ ಸಾಪೇಕ್ಷ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ m/n ನ ಮಿತಿ. ಸ್ವಯಂಸಿದ್ಧ: P(A) ≥ 0, P(S) = 1, ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).

say.en: Classical Laplace: if an experiment has n exhaustive, mutually exclusive and equally likely outcomes, m of which favour A, then PA equals m over n. Statistical von Mises: PA = \lim n\to\infty m over n, the limit of the relative frequency in n repeated trials. Axiomatic Kolmogorov: PA \ge 0, PS equals 1, and P(A \cup B) equals PA plus PB for mutually exclusive A, B. Classical needs equally likely cases.
say.kn: ಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯ: n ಸಮಸಂಭವ, ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ, ಸಮಗ್ರ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ m ಅನುಕೂಲವಾದರೆ PA equals m over n. ಸಾಂಖ್ಯಿಕ: ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಅನಂತದತ್ತ ಸಾಗಿದಾಗ ಸಾಪೇಕ್ಷ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ m over n ನ ಮಿತಿ. ಸ್ವಯಂಸಿದ್ಧ: PA is greater than or equal to 0, PS equals 1, ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ PA union B equals PA plus PB.

say.en: Statistical needs many repetitions.
0 is less than or equal to PA is less than or equal to 1; P(A′) equals 1 - PA.
Classical: count favourable cases over total cases. For sum seven with two dice it is six out of thirty-six.
Statistical: toss a coin again and again. The proportion of heads wobbles at first, then settles near one half.
Axiomatic: three rules every probability must obey.
With combinations: two balls from five red and three black. Both red: five choose two over eight choose two, which is five fourteenths.

problem.en: Two dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum is (a) 7, (b) at least 10.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Two dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum is (a) 7, (b) at least 10.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Two dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum is a 7, b at least 10.
n equals 36.
a Sum 7: 6 cases, P equals 6 over 36 equals 1 over 6.
b Sum 10, 11, 12: 3 plus 2 plus 1 equals 6 cases, P equals 6 over 36 equals 1 over 6.
So the answer is 1 over 6 and 1 over 6.

problem.en: A bag has 5 red and 3 black balls. Two are drawn at random. Find P(both red) and P(one of each colour).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A bag has 5 red and 3 black balls. Two are drawn at random. Find P(both red) and P(one of each colour).

say.en: Let us work this out together. A bag has 5 red and 3 black balls. Two are drawn at random. Find Pboth red and Pone of each colour.
n equals C(8, 2) equals 28.
Both red: C(5, 2) equals 10, so P equals 10 over 28 equals 5 over 14.
One of each: 5 times 3 equals 15, so P equals 15 over 28.
So the answer is 5 over 14 and 15 over 28.
